strengths: The paper addresses an important question: which latent factors multimodal contrastive learning can recover. Separating coupled factors from modality-specific variation is a useful modeling starting point.
Synthetic experiments examine multiple distributions and latent geometries, including assumption violations, and report R² and MCC over three runs.

The CLIP postprocessing pipeline is simple and receives broad downstream evaluation. Reported improvements include increasing ViT-B/16's average accuracy on the four ImageNet target distributions from 32.51% to 37.13% in the two-shot setting.
weaknesses: The central proof contains a fundamental error. Appendix D.1, Lemma 5.1 claims that the minimum normalized contrastive loss is zero. Under the paper's uniform-circle/vMF model with k = τ = 1, identity latent mappings and cosine distance instead yield approximately -0.421. Furthermore, its condition that paired embeddings agree almost surely forces collapse under the full-support vMF conditional, contradicting the simultaneous uniformity requirement. Consequently, the argument establishing a shared encoder mapping and removal of modality-specific variables fails; both main identifiability guarantees depend on this argument.

The convex-body proof has an additional substantive error. Appendix E.1 uses an exactly uniform text-side marginal in Eq. (43), although Lemma 4.2 only asserts convergence to uniformity as λ approaches zero. For finite λ, a truncated Laplace conditional on an interval generally produces a nonuniform marginal because its normalization depends on the source location. The stated cross-entropy reduction therefore does not follow. Corollary 4.4 also omits the restriction to particular non-Euclidean norms introduced only in Appendix E.2.

The FastICA justification is incompatible with the spherical prior. Coordinates of a uniformly distributed spherical vector are dependent because their squared values sum to one, and rotational invariance prevents ICA from identifying a preferred orthogonal orientation. Having M−1 intrinsic degrees of freedom does not supply independent linear sources. The proposed local-isometry justification for PCA followed by ICA is also an unsupported approximation, rather than a disentanglement guarantee.

The causal contribution is insufficiently established. Leaving the relationship between two latent variables undirected describes statistical dependence without specifying intervention semantics or identifying causal structure. The joint distribution can still be factorized in either DAG direction. Much of the subsequent identifiability machinery explicitly reuses Zimmermann et al. [67], making a correct and clearly distinguished multimodal extension essential to the novelty claim.

The downstream experiments do not isolate disentanglement as the mechanism behind improvements. FastICA changes dimensionality and whitening, but matched PCA-only and whitening-only controls are absent. Orthogonal rotations preserve dot products and the optimum of an L2-regularized linear probe, so these evaluations cannot attribute improvements to ICA's disentangling rotation without such controls.

The evidence does not substantiate empirical identifiability. Selected CelebA traversals and classification improvements are insufficient to demonstrate component-wise recovery; quantitative attribute selectivity and stability measurements are missing. Moreover, Appendix K predicts learned representations from true latents when computing R². A rank-deficient linear representation can score perfectly under this evaluation while discarding latent factors, so high R² does not establish invertible recovery.

Reproducibility and reporting need substantial improvement. Synthetic sample counts, batch sizes, optimization schedules, and complete architecture specifications are missing; real-data results lack uncertainty estimates and a sufficiently explicit ICA-fitting protocol. No code resource is provided. There is also a consequential arithmetic error in Figure 4: the RN101 baseline target accuracies average to 22.03%, not the reported 20.03%, overstating the improvement.
